newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES MIXED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES MIXED.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market opened liquid on Monday with short-term trading rates quoted mixed though dealers predicted they would harden in October on the back of reduced volumes of maturities.
"People think rates might go up in October so every one is selling but few people are willing to buy paper at the moment," commented one dealer.
On Monday morning, dealers were purchasing treasury bills from the central Reserve Bank at a stable 22.64 percent but were selling them easier at 22.35 from 22.50 percent.

NCD bills with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 24 percent, up from 23.75 percent but sold at a softer 22.75 from 23 percent while bankers acceptance bills were at 23.5 and 22.35 percent from 22.75 percent and 22.50 percent.
Call money was quoted unchanged at 22 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated a market surplus of Z$206 million at market opening.
